items.title: Gemini for Mac gets Computer Use: multi-step clicking, typing and form-filling across your desktop apps
items.summary: The Gemini app for Mac can now carry out multi-step actions — clicking, typing, filling forms — across desktop apps and websites, in its own separate window. You choose which apps it can use, and it pauses for logins or payments. Rolling out in English to Google AI Plus, Pro and Ultra subscribers (18+, personal accounts) in the U.S.
items.why: A real computer-use agent shipped into a mainstream desktop app, not a research demo.
items.action: If eligible, download the Gemini Mac app and give it one bounded multi-app task to see where it draws the confirmation line.

items.title: Vercel ships Board: a shared message board where agents (and you) coordinate tasks
items.summary: An experimental primitive: a message board of channels and threads where agents claim tasks, post updates, and complete work via a CLI or SDK, with two-way Slack/GitHub sync, per-channel access grants, and task dependencies for swarm coordination. items.why: A real attempt at the missing shared coordination layer for multi-agent setups, not another single-agent harness.

items.title: Simon Willison: Gemini 4 Hydrogen's thinking-effort setting is a bigger lever than people realize
items.summary: Comparing a fixed test at "high" vs "xhigh" thinking effort on Gemini 4 Hydrogen, the xhigh run cost about 6x the tokens and price of the high run for the same prompt.
items.why: A concrete reminder that the reasoning-effort setting, not just model choice, is a major cost/quality lever.

items.title: LangSmith Tool Gateway: one managed layer for credentials, access and audit across every agent's tools
items.summary: A public-beta managed layer that puts every agent tool call behind identity, access and audit controls: register MCP servers or built-ins, group tools into scoped "kits," choose identity mode (as the user or as the agent), and apply deny/approval policies, with every call traced. An anonymized large retailer runs it across 50+ MCP servers and 1,000+ tools.
items.why: The access-control and audit layer most homegrown MCP setups are missing.
items.action: Map which of your own MCP tools are reachable by every agent today with no per-tool scoping, and note the first one you'd want a deny policy on.
